input.rationale: The extended-window fact was supplemented this run with a second execution, and its statement still reads as one execution's numbers: it says the confirmation returns nil again at 5509ms and that the control returns leadership loss at 20003ms, which are the latencies of the first receipt only, while the second execution returned the second confirmation at 4928ms and its control at 20007ms and a third repeat returned 5398ms and 20002ms. I am correcting the statement of that entry under its own id so its content matches the receipts it cites, without changing what it is a fact about: in this configuration the second confirmation arrives several seconds after the partition while a competing leader already leads, and the control's error arrives when the lease expires. No recorded use depends on the exact milliseconds (the entry has no recorded uses, and the interpretations cite the indices rather than the latencies), so the correction is confined to the entry's own statement.

knowledge.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil immediately after the partition, and answers nil again several seconds later (4928ms, 5398ms and 5509ms in the executions recorded) at a moment when one of the far nodes is already Leader while L is still Leader, with that far node having committed a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L at applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" when L's 20s lease expires (20002ms, 20003ms and 20007ms in the executions recorded).
knowledge.conditions: Real 4-node in-memory cluster, only L bootstrapped; near node demoted voter->non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API; transport routes between {L, C} and {far1, far2} removed in both directions; CommitTimeout 200ms; leader lease 20s.
knowledge.changed_premise: The statement previously presented the latencies of a single execution (5509ms and 20003ms) as the fact's content while the entry cites three executions whose latencies differ; it now reports the observed range across those executions and keeps the same subject, conditions and sources.

knowledge.statement: On a leader, verifyLeader() registers the pending verifyFuture on every entry of leaderState.replState and compares accumulated votes against a quorum size computed only from voters; every followerReplication whose AppendEntries/heartbeat response reports success calls notifyAll(true), which increments verifyFuture.votes without consulting the peer's ServerSuffrage. Therefore a peer recorded as Nonvoter (or Staging) contributes a vote to the VerifyLeader confirmation.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the peer is present in r.configurations.latest.Servers with Suffrage != Voter and is reachable by the leader's transport; the verifyFuture is still pending (notifyCh != nil) when the response arrives.

knowledge.statement: In a real 4-node in-memory cluster whose latest configuration has voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter reachable by the leader, a VerifyLeader call issued immediately after the leader is cut off from far1 and far2 returns nil (success) with the leader still in Leader state, within the same millisecond as the partition, in three independent attempts on each of two receipts. Repeating the identical scenario with that reachable node still a voter, or with the non-voter also unreachable, returns "leadership lost while committing log" about one LeaderLeaseTimeout later instead.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; latest configuration voters=3, nonvoters=1 (quorum_size=voters/2+1=2); transport routes to the two far voters removed while routes to the non-voter stay intact; HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout (3s treatment, 2s controls), ProtocolVersion 3; in-memory transport and stores in one process.

knowledge.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil at 0ms after the partition, and answers nil again at 5509ms when one of the far nodes is already Leader, while that node commits a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L still Leader, applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" at 20003ms, when L's lease expires.
knowledge.conditions: Real 4-node in-memory cluster, only L bootstrapped; near node demoted voter->non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API; transport routes between {L, C} and {far1, far2} removed in both directions; CommitTimeout 200ms; leader lease 20s.

history.statement: With voters {L, far1, far2} and non-voter C, per-node timing (L: HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; far1, far2: 3s; C: 6s) and the partition {L, C} | {far1, far2}: L answers VerifyLeader with nil at 0ms after the partition, and answers nil again at 5509ms when one of the far nodes is already Leader, while that node commits a write at index 5 that L's FSM lacks (L still Leader, applied index 3). With the same per-node timing but C still a voter (four voters, quorum 3) no competitor can appear and the same call returns "leadership lost while committing log" at 20003ms, when L's lease expires.
history.conditions: Real 4-node in-memory cluster, only L bootstrapped; near node demoted voter->non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API; transport routes between {L, C} and {far1, far2} removed in both directions; CommitTimeout 200ms; leader lease 20s; single execution.

knowledge.statement: In a healthy 4-node cluster (leader HeartbeatTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s, the node to be demoted 6s, the two far voters 3s, only the leader bootstrapped) a committed DemoteVoter transition is reflected in every node's own GetConfiguration view of that peer's suffrage within 0-20ms of the leader's commit, measured every 20ms for ten seconds, in four runs; no node's view was still old at a sample where its own LastIndex had already reached the configuration entry's index.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-memory transports, no partition, no load, no restart; the transition is a single DemoteVoter call on the leader with prevIndex 0; followers are otherwise caught up (LastIndex >= 2) before the change in the successor runs.

knowledge.statement: In a 4-node cluster whose configuration is voters {leader, far1, far2} plus one Nonvoter, LeadershipTransferToServer aimed at the non-voter returns success (nil) within about a millisecond while the sitting leader is already Follower and the named destination is only Candidate; the destination never leads during the following eight seconds and the cluster is observed without a leader at some 20ms sample before a different node wins the fresh election. With the identical call aimed at a voter, success is returned in about three milliseconds, the named destination leads, and no leaderless sample occurs.
knowledge.conditions: Real in-memory transports, fully connected, uniform HeartbeatTimeout 2s and LeaderLeaseTimeout 1s, CommitTimeout 200ms; the non-voter is produced by DemoteVoter before the transfer; one execution of each case.

result.summary: Corrected the one promoted item whose content no longer matched its receipts. The extended-window fact quoted a single execution's latencies (5509ms for the second confirmation, 20003ms for the control) while now citing three executions whose values are 4928/5398/5509ms and 20002/20003/20007ms, so its statement now reports the observed range and keeps the same subject, conditions, sources and executions; the correction is filed under the entry's own id with changed_premise explaining the difference, and no recorded use depended on the exact milliseconds since the interpretations cite parsed indices rather than latencies. That leaves the run coherent and complete: three settled lines, each with fixed experiments, retained receipts, current interpretations and promoted knowledge (VerifyLeader confirmable by a non-voter's acknowledgement for the whole configured lease with the voter-only lease as the bound, asserted; the demotion-view lag refuted and closed; LeadershipTransferToServer to a non-voter reporting success while the sitting leadership is interrupted and a fresh election decides, asserted), plus one open, owned gap about the unexplained divergence of the near_node_self_voter field, which no claim in the run depends on. Nothing further was submitted, since the remaining allocation is shorter than a construction, execution and interpretation cycle.
